cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where error pages incorporate user-controllable data (error messages, stack traces, query parameters) into HTML responses without proper output encoding, leading to cross-site scripting or information disclosure, as well as a memory exhaustion issue from unbounded caching of attacker-influenced error pages.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Apply HTML escaping to the data (e.g., using StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 or HtmlEscapers) before inserting it into the HTML template..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Missing HTML escaping of user-controllable error content leading to XSS
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Apply HTML escaping to the data (e.g., using StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 or HtmlEscapers) before inserting it into the HTML template.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Apply HTML escaping to the data (e.g., using StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 or HtmlEscapers) before inserting it into the HTML template.
sub_patterns.name: Missing HTML escaping of user-controllable error content leading to XSS
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled data (error messages or exception stack traces) is embedded directly into an HTML response without HTML entity encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML/JavaScript.
